chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muawiya ibn Maythara, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Or he was asked: Does the man pray while sitting in the Mutarabb' position with both legs spread out? He said: 'There is no harm (in it).'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm; it is permissible or acceptable.
key_terms.مَبْسُوطَ الرَّجْلَيْنِ: With both legs spread out or extended.
key_terms.مُتَرَبِّعاً: A sitting posture where the knees are raised, often with one foot upright and the other flat against the ground.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray sitting with legs spread out in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of the 'Mutarabb'' sitting posture during prayer, a position often associated with comfort or modesty in the Prophet's time. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of ease (taysir), distinguishing this specific sitting style from postures that might imply disrespect or distraction, thereby affirming its validity for both obligatory and voluntary prayers.
